item.title: 🤖 The AnnounceKit MCP Server is Here: Your Changelog Now Ships Itself
item.description: Connect Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or any AI agent to AnnounceKit over MCP. Your AI can now draft, update, publish, and schedule announcements, reply to feature requests, manage your roadmap, and read your stats - straight from a chat.
item.content:encoded:
Big one today. AnnounceKit now ships an official MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, and it changes how product updates get announced: your AI assistant can now run your changelog for you.

Ask Claude to announce what you just shipped. Have Cursor draft release notes from a merged PR. Let ChatGPT summarize this week's feedback and reply to the top feature request. It all happens in your chat, and lands in your changelog, widgets, email, and Slack.

⚡ Connect in two minutes

Hosted (recommended) - nothing to install. Add this URL to your AI client as a custom connector, then log in and approve:

https://mcp.announcekit.app/mcp

In Claude: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector. Cursor, ChatGPT (Developer Mode), and any MCP-compatible client work the same way.

Local (for developers) - run it yourself with npx announcekit-mcp and an API token from Settings → API Tokens.

🛠 What your AI can do

  • Posts: list, read, draft, update, publish, and schedule announcements
  • Feedback & feature requests: read feedback, create, comment on, and reply to requests
  • Roadmap: read the roadmap, add items and statuses
  • Insights: read post stats and NPS

🔒 Safe by design

The MCP server is read and create/update/publish only. There are no delete actions and no billing access - those stay in the dashboard. Tokens are scoped (read or write), act at the creating member's role, and you can review or revoke every connection under Settings → Connected apps. Prefer a human in the loop? Have your agent save drafts and publish them yourself.

💡 Try these prompts first

  • "Announce what we shipped in this issue. Match the tone of our last posts."
  • "Draft the v2 launch announcement and schedule it for Tuesday 9am."
  • "Summarize this week's feedback, then reply to the top feature request with our plan."
  • "How did last week's posts perform?"

📚 Learn more

  • The MCP experience - see agents working your changelog, live
  • Changelog automation - the full use case, step by step
  • MCP setup docs - hosted and local setup, tokens, troubleshooting

P.S. This announcement was drafted over the AnnounceKit MCP server by an AI agent. It works. 🙂

item.title: We're ending support for older TLS versions (1.0 and 1.1)
item.description: We're always working to keep your traffic to AnnounceKit secure. In line with current security and industry best practices, we are phasing o...
item.content:encoded:
We're always working to keep your traffic to AnnounceKit secure. In line with current security and industry best practices, we are phasing out legacy TLS protocols - specifically TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1.

Effective date:  30 Apr 2026

What's changing

Starting on that date, AnnounceKit will only accept connections using TLS 1.2 or newer.

Will this affect me?

Most modern browsers and operating systems already use TLS 1.2+, so you typically won't need to do anything. You might only run into issues if you use very old browsers, legacy mobile devices, or sit behind corporate proxies that don't negotiate TLS 1.2 or higher.

What should you do?

Keep your browser and OS up to date. If you're on a corporate network, ask your IT team to confirm that TLS 1.2+ is enabled for outbound HTTPS traffic.

If you have questions or run into connectivity issues after the change, contact us at support@announcekit.com

Thank you,

AnnounceKit Team
